newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse media profit falls in second quarter.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse media profit falls in second quarter.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp. Monday reported a $1 million profit for the second quarter after recording a loss of $89 million in the year-earlier period.
But operating profits at its core media business fell from the prior period.

Westinghouse, which plans to split its CBS broadcasting business from its industrial power and technology business in the fall, said the quarterly profit, equal to nil per share, came on revenues of $2.4 billion, up from $2.1 billion a year earlier. The loss in the 1996 quarter equalled 20 cents a share, when the company took an after-tax charge of $114 million, or 26 cents per share.

Westinghouse said operating profit in the media business fell almost 20 percent, to $155 million from $192 million. That was despite a nearly 17 percent gain in total media sales, to $1.28 billion from $1.10 billion.

For the latest quarter, Westinghouse said its media group, which includes the CBS television and radio networks, as well as Infinity Broadcasting, reported earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $261 million. That compared with $340 million in the year-earlier quarter, on a proforma basis.

Infinity's contribution for the quarter was offset by decreased revenue at the television network and a less favourable effect of purchase price accounting for programme rights. On a proforma basis, sales in the media group were essentially flat.
CBS Radio posted EBITDA of $157 million, about 23 percent above a year ago on a proforma basis. But television stations revenues declined 4 percent on a comparable station basis.

"We expect our ongoing growth, particularly in the major markets, to benefit significantly from greater interaction among our television, radio and outdoor businesses," said Michael Jordan, chairman and chief executive officer.
During the quarter, the company combined its radio and television groups into a consolidated CBS Station Group, and took several steps to improve advertising sales in its local markets.

Westinghouse said its Power Systems business boosted revenues to $838 million in the latest quarter, versus $732 million a year earlier. It squeezed out operating profits of $1 million versus a loss of $35 million.

The Thermo King transport refrigeration unit posted operating profits of $49 million on revenue of $263 million, versus $46 million on $265 million in sales a year earlier. The company said profitability in the unit was enhanced by a surge in bus air conditioning sales, improved conditions in the North American truck and trailer industry, lower material costs and productivity improvements.

Westinghouse said financial performance improved in every business in its Industries and Technology Group. Total revenues increased 14 percent, primarily due to increased service sales in the Power Generation unit.
Westinghouse's stock slipped 6.25 cents to $24.3125 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
